prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1014; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy file and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the incident. Nothing in the file suggests any issue with the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report and spoke with two witnesses, who both confirm the accident happened as described and that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. Photos submitted by the parties are consistent with these accounts.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle damage, which lines up well with the impact described by the parties. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior records or the inspection.

Entry 5: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account matching the claimant's. The claimant has repeated the same account in every conversation so far, with no changes in the details.

Entry 6: Medical records show neck and back strain. The reported injury fits the kind and force of the collision, and no prior injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved. Based on the records and the damage, the claim is progressing normally and remains open pending final medical updates from counsel.
